papers.title: Research Progress of T Cell Metabolism in Graft-Versus-Host Disease.
papers.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a common and severe complication following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). It is caused by activated alloreactive T cells that attack recipient target organs and represents a major cause of non-relapse mortality, thereby limiting the efficacy of allo-HSCT. Persistent alloantigen stimulation can induce metabolic dysregulation in T cells, involving pathways such as glycolysis, lipid metabolism, amino acid metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. Given the close relationship between T cell metabolism and T cell activation, differentiation, and effector functions, targeted modulation of T cell metabolism may emerge as a novel strategy for the prevention and treatment of GVHD. This review summarizes the roles of major T cell metabolic pathways in the pathogenesis and progression of GVHD with the aim of informing future mechanistic studies and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég' Xdaltth'í' and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska.
papers.abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia's archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég' Xdaltth'í' site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég' Xdaltth'í' represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia's oldest site, Shég' Xdaltth'í' reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

papers.title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum.
papers.abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

papers.title: Geochronology and geochemistry of granitic dikes in the Xiaogushan gold deposit NE China and implications for gold mineralization.
papers.abstract: The Xiaogushan cryptoexplosive breccia-type gold deposit is located within the eastern Hebei-western Liaoning gold belt along the northern margin of the North China Craton. The mining area contains multiple episodes of subvolcanic dikes, among which the granite porphyry and granitic aplite dikes show close temporal and spatial relationship with gold mineralization. To constrain their emplacement age, petrogenesis, tectonic setting, and metallogenic significance, integrated zircon U-Pb-Hf isotopic and whole‑rock geochemical analyses were carried out on these dikes. Zircon U-Pb dating yields emplacement ages of 163.9 ± 2.0 Ma for the granite porphyry and 162.2 ± 4.9 Ma for the granitic aplite, indicating Late Jurassic magmatism in the region. The rocks are enriched in SiO2, K2O, and LILEs, depleted in HFSEs, and classified as strongly peraluminous, high‑K calc‑alkaline S‑type granites. The primary magma, derived from Paleoproterozoic lower crust (εHf(t) = -17.7 to -13.5; TDM2 = 2.29 to 2.07 Ga), and the geochemical variations are consistent with fractional crystallization of K‑feldspar and plagioclase. Regional tectonic evidence indicates that these dikes were emplaced in a continental collisional setting related to the closure of the Mongol‑Okhotsk Ocean. This collision caused crustal thickening, deformation, and subsequent extension, which promoted mineralization. These dikes characterized by high oxygen fugacity, alkali enrichment, and moderate evolution, may facilitate metal transport and remobilize pre‑existing mineralization via associated hydrothermal systems. Their clustered occurrence thus serves as a potential indicator for deep‑seated hydrothermal activity and gold mineralization, reflecting the intense Mesozoic tectono-magmatic-metallogenic event in the northern North China Craton.

papers.title: Ball-milling medium dictates the reconstruction pathway of hydrochar: Coupling pore opening with functionality retention.
papers.abstract: Hydrochar retains abundant oxygen-containing functional groups but little porosity, and thermal upgrading opens pores at the expense of surface chemistry. Ball milling requires no external heating, so its structural outcome is decided by how freshly fragmented particles reorganize. Here, dry and water-mediated ball milling of corn-straw hydrochar were compared to resolve how the milling medium directs this reorganization, with 600℃ biochar as a thermal reference. Without a liquid phase, fragments recontacted and densified: the specific surface area fell from 11.23 to 2.91 m2·g-1, the total pore volume from 0.0818 to 0.0179 cm3·g-1, and the CO proportion from 26.2 % to 19.0 %, so pore closure and carbonyl loss occurred together. In water, dispersion suppressed reagglomeration, increasing the specific surface area, total pore volume, and CO proportion to 34.26 m2·g-1, 0.1903 cm3·g-1, and 33.3 %, respectively. HTC-WBM adsorbed 2.53, 2.41, and 3.15 times as much TC as HTC, HTC-DBM, and BC, respectively. Although BC had the highest specific surface area (54.99 m2·g-1), its total pore volume and BET-equivalent average pore diameter were only 0.0439 cm3·g-1 and 3.19 nm, compared with 0.1903 cm3·g-1 and 22.22 nm for HTC-WBM. Open meso-/macropores facilitated TC transport to retained oxygen-containing sites, where hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions contributed to adsorption. Spectroscopic evidence and SHAP analysis were consistent with this coupled pore-accessibility/functionality effect. Medium-controlled milling therefore couples pore opening with functionality retention.

papers.title: Surface-engineered cationic silver nanoparticles as a selective colorimetric sensor for mercury(II) detection in environmental water.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.abstract: Synthesis of silver (Ag) nanoparticles was done using chemical reduction of AgNO3 in ice cold NaBH4, and functionalization of the surface was done using cysteamine via Ag-S thiolate bonding at pH 9.0. Quaternization of the surface was achieved via exhaustive N-methylation of the terminal amine group at the surface using iodomethane (CH3I). This converts the surface -NH2 groups stepwise into permanently positively charged quaternary ammonium moieties (-N+(CH3)3). The resulting surface-modified nanoparticles (AgNPs-QCy) were comprehensively characterized using UV-visible spectroscopy, Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy-Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX), Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS), and zeta potential measurements. Surface quaternization was confirmed by the red shift in the Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) band from ∼385 nm to 393 nm, attributed to changes in the local dielectric environment at the nanoparticle surface following quaternization, and accompanied by a decrease in the hydrodynamic diameter from 314.2 nm to 149.9 nm, consistent with improved colloidal uniformity upon surface charge stabilization. Zeta potential measurements confirmed the pH-independent positive surface charge, thus confirming the stability of the permanent quaternary ammonium group over a broad range of pH. AgNPs-QCy exhibited high selectivity toward Hg2+ ions in the presence of several competing metal ions, including Fe2+, Zn2+, Cd2+, Mn2+, Pb2+, Al3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Cu2+, As5+, Cr3+, and La3+. The selective response toward Hg2+ is attributed to its strong interaction with the functionalized AgNP surface, leading to pronounced changes in nanoparticle interfacial interactions and plasmonic properties. These changes result in aggregation and suppression of the LSPR signal, producing a distinct colorimetric response that can be visually observed. AgNPs-QCy-based sensor

papers.title: Relationship quality and subjective well-being of persons with dementia and partners: A systematic review using a resilience framework.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to explore changes in relationship quality between persons with dementia and their partners and examine the association of relationship quality with subjective well-being. METHODS: Eleven databases were systematically searched from inception to November 2024, along with manual screening of reference lists. Selected studies were critically appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Convergent integrated approach was used to synthesize findings based on the resilience framework. The GRADE-CERQual approach was applied to assess confidence in the synthesised qualitative evidence. RESULTS: This synthesis included 10 qualitative, 10 quantitative, and 4 mixed-method studies. Within a resilience framework, 18 initial categories were distilled into three themes and nine subthemes. Relationship quality changes between persons with dementia and their partners unfold across three empirically derived stages: maintenance, adjustment, and redefinition. Influencing factors encompass individual factors such as disease knowledge and initiative, family factors such as beliefs, reciprocity, and communication, and social factors, such as social support services and neighbourhood context. Overall, higher relationship quality is associated with higher subjective well-being. CONCLUSION: Dyadic relationship quality is significantly associated with the subjective well-being of both persons with dementia and their partners. Resilience factors should be integrated into interventions to enhance relationship quality and promote mutual subjective well-being.

papers.title: Integrating Family-Based Treatment Components Into CBT-E for Adolescent Eating Disorders: A Narrative Review and Proposal for Family-Enhanced CBT-E (CBT-FE).
papers.journal: The International journal of eating disorders
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Family-based treatment (FBT) and Enhanced Cognitive Behavior Therapy (CBT-E) are two leading evidence-based outpatient approaches for adolescent eating disorders, but their strengths and limitations may be partly complementary. This review critically examines both approaches and proposes a structured integration termed Family-Enhanced CBT-E (CBT-FE). METHOD: The theoretical foundations, treatment structures, evidence base, and limitations of FBT and adolescent CBT-E were narratively reviewed, with particular attention to parental involvement, cognitive maintaining mechanisms, weight restoration, treatment engagement, and developmental considerations. RESULTS: CBT-FE retains the four-phase structure, personalized formulation, and core intervention strategies of CBT-E as the treatment backbone while incorporating formulation-driven parent and family components adapted from FBT. These include a non-blaming stance, externalization, parental empowerment, structured meal support, and gradual transfer of responsibility for eating. Parental involvement is conceptualized as a flexible "dose" calibrated according to the adolescent's age, insight, weight status, clinical needs, and family capacity, and progressively reduced as treatment advances. DISCUSSION: CBT-FE does not alter the first-line status of family therapy: it is intended for adolescents in whom individual treatment is indicated or chosen and structures family involvement within that treatment from the start. It is a conceptual proposal intended to preserve adolescent agency and CBT-E's direct targeting of maintaining mechanisms while mobilizing family resources when clinically indicated. Its feasibility, acceptability, and effectiveness require prospective evaluation in open trials and randomized controlled studies.

papers.title: Dyadic Associations between Body Appreciation and Sexual Function among Cisgender Heterosexual and Gender and Sexually Diverse Couples.
papers.abstract: Given the body's exposure during partnered sexual activity, having a positive perception of one's body may impact sexual function, i.e., the capacity to respond sexually. Yet research on the associations between body appreciation and sexual function within couples is limited, particularly among couples who identify as gender and sexually diverse, who face greater risks of experiencing sexual difficulties due to minority stress. Examining body appreciation among couples may lead to clearer insights into their sexual function. The present study assessed dyadic associations between body appreciation and sexual function, examining the moderating effects of gender identity and sexual orientation, in a diverse sample of 151 couples. Results based on the actor-partner interdependence moderation model showed that a person's body appreciation was negatively related to their own sexual function difficulties, and to their partner's difficulties when the latter was heterosexual. Gender identity did not significantly moderate these associations. This study demonstrates the associations between a person's body appreciation and their own sexual function, as well as the role of the partner's sexual orientation in the association between a person's body appreciation and their partner's sexual function, highlighting the importance of considering sexual orientation to understand dyadic associations with sexual health.

papers.title: Dental Student Perceived Preparedness to Work With Diverse Patients.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE/OBJECTIVES: The US patient population has become increasingly diverse with complex needs and lived experiences. To address existing gaps in dental education, this study explored dental students' self-reported preparedness to provide care to patients with diverse needs and suggestions to enhance the curriculum. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey developed by an interdisciplinary team was administered to D1-D4 dental students to assess perceived preparedness to work with patients across diverse social, cultural, and clinical contexts. Open-ended items solicited recommendations for curricular improvement. Descriptive statistics summarized preparedness ratings. Independent-samples t-tests compared pre-clinical (D1-D2) and clinical (D3-D4) students. Open-text responses were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: Of 394 eligible students, 187 completed the survey (47.5% response rate), with 113 included in the final analytic sample. On 1-10 scale, students reported moderate preparedness across all diverse identities and experiences, with the lowest preparedness in caring for survivors of sexual violence (M = 4.51), intimate partner violence (M = 4.62), trauma (M = 4.83), and patients with special healthcare needs (M = 4.54), and the highest for patients differing by sexual orientation (M = 7.30), race (M = 7.18), and culture (M = 6.91). Clinical students reported significantly higher preparedness than pre-clinical students across most diverse identities and experiences. Qualitative responses (N = 40) identified recommendations to enhance the curriculum, including opportunities for: (1) Experiential learning, (2) cultural humility, (3) structured communication training, and (4) mentorship/interprofessional education. CONCLUSIONS: Findings demonstrate that dental students reported feeling least prepared to work with patients who have trauma-related experiences and special health care needs, indicating a gap in the areas of greatest complexity and need. papers.title: The Influence of Perpetrator's Substance Use on Survivor's Use of Protective Strategies: Findings from a Daily Diary Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Men's substance use influences their intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetration and women's assessment of their IPV-related risk. Women actively protect themselves using various strategies to stop, prevent, or escape conflict in their relationship. This study examines whether perpetrators' use of substances is related to women's daily protective strategy use. METHODS: Women (N = 216, Mage = 40.7 years [SD = 13.1], 34.7% Black, 26.9% White) experiencing physical or repeated psychological IPV were recruited from the community and completed once-daily app-based surveys for 90 days, in which they reported their partner's alcohol, cannabis, and other drug use, and their own protective strategy use. Generalized linear mixed models were used to test study hypotheses. RESULTS: Partner substance use was associated with increased likelihood of women's same-day creating distance, preparing to leave, weapons-related, and placating strategy use (ps < 0.001). Partner's alcohol use alone was related to increased likelihood of same-day creating distance, preparing to leave, and placating strategy use (ps ≤ 0.006), alcohol-cannabis co-use was related to increased likelihood of same-day placating strategy use (p < 0.001), and any other drug use was related to increased likelihood of same-day creating distance and placating strategy use (ps ≤ 0.002). Partner's cannabis use alone was related to decreased likelihood of using preparing to leave strategies the next day (p = 0.04), whereas any other drug use was related to increased likelihood of next-day creating distance, preparing to leave, and placating strategy use (ps ≤ 0.02). DISCUSSION: Partner substance use is a contextual factor that may have important implications for IPV intervention programming and formal safety planning efforts with women experiencing IPV.

papers.title: State Variation in the Availability of Women-Specific Alcohol Use Disorder Treatment.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In the United States (U.S.), the prevalence of alcohol use disorder (AUD) is increasing among women; however, few women seek treatment. System-level information on the need for AUD treatment among women and the availability of services relevant to women is essential to ensure that women have access to care. This study describes state variation in the number of addiction treatment facilities serving clients with AUD per 10 000 women with AUD, state variation in treatment facilities offering women-specific programming, and services that address commonly cited barriers to treatment, and estimates the availability of women-specific programming and services in states with disproportionately higher AUD prevalence among women. METHODS: Using the 2024 National Substance Use and Mental Health Services Survey data, this study identified the number of addiction treatment facilities that offered women-specific programming and services addressing frequently cited treatment barriers for women and estimated the 2024 proportion of facilities with these services per 10 000 women aged 18+ with AUD by state. RESULTS: State-level prevalence estimates of AUD among women ranged from 6.2% to 12.7%. Of the 13 818 treatment facilities in the U.S. offering alcohol treatment, 58.5% offered women-specific programming, 59.0% offered trauma therapy, 55.4% offered intimate partner violence services, 55.2% offered transportation assistance, and 4.6% offered childcare. States with a higher proportion of women with AUD had fewer alcohol treatment facilities offering women-specific programming per woman with AUD. CONCLUSIONS: There is state-level variation in the availability of facilities offering women-specific programming and services. Of concern, many states with greater than average AUD prevalence had disproportionately lower availability of services.

papers.title: Integrating Chlamydia and Gonorrhea Testing into a Community-Based Cohort of Latine Young Adults: Patterns and Predictors of Uptake.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: We examined STI testing behaviors in a community-based study that removed access and cost barriers by offering in-person and mail-in testing. METHODS: A Crecer is a prospective cohort study of adolescents and young adults in an agricultural, majority Latine community (2015-2025). STI testing was offered at three annual visits in emerging adulthood (2022-2025). Participants provided biospecimens for chlamydia/gonorrhea testing, either in-person or via mailed self-collection kit, and completed questionnaires. We examined associations between individual, relationship, and environmental factors and STI testing using Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: Participants (N=389, 56% female sex at birth, 95% Latine) had a mean age of 20 (range 18-22). Sixty-three percent tested at the first visit in early adulthood, decreasing to 44% and 33% in subsequent annual visits. Initial uptake was higher among those completing in-person versus remote visits (84% vs. 25%). Chlamydia prevalence was 8% at the first visit in early adulthood, and positivity was 5% and 2% at subsequent visits. Testing did not vary by sex. In multivariable analysis, uptake was higher among those experiencing intimate partner violence (adjusted Relative Risk (aRR): 1.3; 95% CI: 1.1, 1.4, p<0.001), and among those reporting sex without a condom in the prior 12 months (aRR: 1.2; CI: 1.0, 1.4, p=0.03). Receipt of sexual health services outside the study was not associated with testing uptake. CONCLUSIONS: While many tested based on perceived STI risk, uptake fell short of public health recommendations. Low uptake of mail-in testing highlights the need for testing models that better align with Latine young adults' preferences and circumstances. Findings underscore the importance of understanding testing barriers and normalizing STI screening as routine preventive care.
